source_title: STARBUCKS CORP - Form 8-K - FY2008 (fiscal 2008 financial results press release exhibit)
company_context: Starbucks Corporation, the global coffee retailer, overexpanded U.S. company-operated stores in the mid-2000s, diluting the customer experience and store-level returns. Howard Schultz returned as CEO in January 2008 and launched a transformation agenda, including closing underperforming stores and slowing U.S. growth.
evidence_summary: For fiscal 2008 (ended September 28, 2008) consolidated net revenues rose 10% to $10.4 billion (from $9.4 billion in FY2007), but comparable store sales fell 3% for the 12 months, driven by the U.S. segment at negative 5% (International was positive 2%). Operating income fell to $504 million from $1.1 billion, and operating margin contracted 630 basis points to 4.9% from 11.2%. In July 2008 Starbucks announced closure of approximately 600 underperforming U.S. company-operated stores, ~70% of which had opened since the start of fiscal 2006, and cut planned U.S. openings to ~1,175 (from a revised target of 1,600) while raising International openings to ~975. Schultz called fiscal 2008 a transitional year and framed the transformation agenda as reinvigorating the Starbucks Experience.
outcome_evidence: Fiscal 2008 showed clear distress (comparable store sales -3%, operating income roughly halved, ~600 U.S. store closures). The transformation agenda under Schultz - closing overexpanded stores, slowing U.S. growth, refocusing on the customer experience - led Starbucks back to growth and margin recovery in subsequent years, a documented operational turnaround (outcome 4).
source_limitations: SEC EDGAR exhibit returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch; all FY2008 figures are quoted verbatim from domain-restricted (sec.gov) search-result snippets of the Starbucks 8-K exhibits. The store-closure details (600 stores, ~70% post-FY2006, revised opening targets) are from a separate FY2008 8-K (July 2008 announcement) corroborated within the same EDGAR filing set. Subsequent-year recovery is from later filings, not this release.
directly_stated: FY2008 net revenues $10.4 billion (+10%) vs $9.4 billion FY2007
operating income $504 million vs $1.1 billion; margin 4.9% vs 11.2%
approximately 600 US store closures announced; ~70% opened since start of FY2006
US openings cut to ~1,175 from revised 1,600; International raised to ~975
inferred: the binding problem was self-inflicted overexpansion (operational/footprint bottleneck), not a pure demand collapse
closing units and slowing growth was the corrective lever restoring store-level economics
why_useful_for_opsiq: Operational over-expansion crisis with quantified margin compression and comparable-sales decline, corrected by store rationalization and refocusing - a documented turnaround. Tests OpsIQ's diagnosis of operational_bottleneck vs demand collapse, and re-evaluation after a major footprint/scope correction.
